a1-s01.text: Seven lamps hang from the woodshed beam; three are lit. The master stands in the doorway and says he has looked at your back: "Sword qi leaks between the bones. You were born with a sword in them." Behind him the second brother mutters: "Don't listen. That's a body forged by hard training. An iron body."

a1-s02-sword.text: Seven old cuts mark the bluestone behind the hill. The master puts a wooden sword in your hand: "Split it, and the sword-bone wakes." You strike; the stone parts, the break flat as a knife cut. The master smiles: "There."
choices: Believe him again. Ask what comes next.
Ask him: if I have a sword-bone, why won't you let me meet the sect head?

a1-s02-body.text: The bricks in the west wall are new. The second brother has you throw a punch: "An iron body doesn't look at swords. It looks at bone." Three bricks shatter; your knuckles only redden. "There," he says. "Done." A length of old straw rope shows in the gap.
choices: Believe him again. Ask what comes next.
Crouch and look at the gap: who replaced these bricks?

a1-s03-sword.text: She nods: "Then do not ask. Keep practising." The master teaches you three sword formulas, each spoken only halfway. You practise them, and at night your back really does run hot. Half a year on you can split three feet of bluestone in one stroke, and the master watches from under the eaves without a word. You remember he never took you to meet the sect head, and that you never asked.

a1-s03-body.text: She tucks the rope into her sleeve: "Then soak the full hundred days." The second brother gives you a jar of medicinal wine and says a hundred days of soaking and the iron body comes by itself. On the seventieth day the whole west wall collapses, opening onto an empty room and a floor of old bricks. He laughs from the doorway and says the courtyard was stacked out of bricks from the start.

a1-s03-turn-sword.text: She pushes the whetstone back a foot: "Good question." You hand the wooden sword back: "You first, master." He does not take it. You ask again: "If I have a sword-bone, what are you afraid of?" His fingers curl inside his sleeve and he turns and walks away. The next day the sect head sends for you — not because you split the stone, but because you asked.

a1-s03-turn-body.text: She puts the rope back in your hand: "Then go ask the brickworks yourself." You crouch and pull the straw rope from the gap; a brickworks mark is tied into it. The second brother's smile stops where it is. You say: "You replaced this wall. You bought the bricks." He does not deny it. He only asks: "So what do you believe now?"

a1-voice-sword-believe.text: The master leaves; only the senior sister stays in the corridor. She pushes the whetstone to your feet: "That sentence in your head, I heard it." You say you said nothing. "I know," she says.
choices: (Inward) He truly wants me to succeed.
(Inward) He is testing me like a blade.

a1-voice-sword-turn.text: After your question the room is quiet for a long time. The master leaves, and the senior sister pulls the door shut: "What you said in your head was crueller than what you said aloud."
choices: (Inward) He truly wants me to succeed.
(Inward) He is testing me like a blade.

a1-voice-body-believe.text: The bricks are knee-high. The second brother goes to call someone to repair the wall. The senior sister crouches and winds the straw rope around her finger: "That sentence in your head, I heard it."
choices: (Inward) He truly wants me to succeed.
(Inward) This courtyard was stacked out of bricks from the start.

a1-voice-body-turn.text: When you finish, the second brother's smile stops on his face and he turns to call for help. The senior sister stays. She takes the rope out of your hand: "What you said in your head was uglier than what you said aloud."
choices: (Inward) He truly wants me to succeed.
(Inward) This courtyard was stacked out of bricks from the start.
